source_documents.title: Kinetics of Excimer Electrogenerated Chemiluminescence of Pyrene and 1-Pyrenebutyricacid 2-Ethylhexylester in Acetonitrile and an Ionic Liquid, Triethylpentylphosphonium Bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide

conditions_studied: MeCN solution, 10 μM to high concentration

reference_evidence_units.quote: Upon light absorption, the excimer emission of PLQ was observed at high concentrations as pyrene, and the kinetics of the excimer formation is limited by diffusion.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Concentration-dependent excimer emission with diffusion-limited formation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: For neat PLQ (1.6 M), a delay of 0.3−0.4 ns for the excimer emission compared to the monomer emission was observed.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Delayed excimer rise in the neat liquid; monomer emission is negligible.

reference_evidence_units.quote: time-dependent DFT calculations show that the potential energy curve of the excimer against the distance between the pyrene rings reaches a minimum at 3.50 Å.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ dimer
reference_evidence_units.statement: Excimer energy minimum at 3.50 Å ring separation.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Because the S1 → S0 transition of pyrene is symmetry forbidden,44 the enhancement of kM r for PLQ is attributable to its less symmetric molecular structure by the presence of the substituent.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ vs pyrene
reference_evidence_units.statement: The larger monomer kr of PLQ is explained by symmetry breaking by the substituent.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Concerns the monomer radiative rate, not the excimer.

reference_evidence_units.quote: can be ascribed to the suppression of vibrational relaxations, as was observed for several dyes in viscous media.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ and pyrene
reference_evidence_units.statement: Slightly lower knr in the viscous ionic liquid.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No specific intramolecular motion is identified.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Kinetic analysis for the electron transfer reaction between the radical ions based on Marcus theory indicates that the electron transfer is limited by the diffusion of the radical ions.
reference_evidence_units.subject: PLQ radical ions
reference_evidence_units.statement: ECL excited states form by electron transfer between electrogenerated radical ions.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Pyrene excimer formation (concentration series, neat-liquid kinetics, dimer calculations) is the central subject in both PL and ECL.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The monomer radiative rate is analysed and its increase over pyrene is explained by the symmetry-forbidden S1→S0 transition being relaxed by the substituent.

mechanism_decisions.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
mechanism_decisions.rationale: The slightly lower knr in the viscous ionic liquid is ascribed to generic suppression of vibrational relaxation (E05); no specific motion is named, so not labelled (guideline §3.3).

mechanism_decisions.label: ICT_TICT_CT
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Not discussed for this molecule in the source.

mechanism_decisions.label: PET_ET
mechanism_decisions.rationale: Electron transfer here is the annihilation of electrogenerated radical ions that creates ECL excited states (E06), not a photoinduced quenching or switching; recorded out of pool.
